video_title: Greeny gives Stephon Castle his flowers 💐 'He's the REASON San Antonio won!' | Get Up

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's improved energy and mindset in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: He clearly went out with a different mindset last night.
quotes.quote: There was no question last night. I don't know if it was a function of the extra days' rest or whatever the factor was. But Victor Wembanyama in the first two games of the series started slowly, he looked a little tentative, suggesting low energy. Whether it's tired or not, I don't know. He clearly went out with a different mindset last night.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's efficiency and impact in Game 3 compared to previous games
quotes.excerpt: Everything he did in this game had more purpose and cleaner four lob dunks.
quotes.quote: I thought his energy level was totally different from the start of the game. If you looked at his stats from Game 1 and 2, he was actually averaging 28 and 10. You're like, 'Wow, that's pretty good numbers. How can you say he's getting anything kept?' Well, he was shooting 40% and he had 10 turnovers and two dunks. That's not how it's getting the done. In this game, he goes 11 of 18, which is obviously much higher efficiency, six assists, only one turnover. Everything he did in this game had more purpose and cleaner four lob dunks in this game. Total different mentality switch.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Spears

text_blocks.speaker: Marcus Spears
text_blocks.text: I do think you have to give a lot of credit to Mitch Johnson and to the guards, right? Because a lot of his 32 points weren't self-created. They were created by other guards. And when you actually think about 28 assists in the game for the Spurs, and just think about this for Wembanyama, which I think is crazy even in this series: plus-10 with him on the court, minus-17 with him off the court.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: The fact that he was able to play the whole fourth quarter without sitting was a huge factor in the game.

quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's impact on Spurs' plus-minus and team-created scoring
quotes.excerpt: Plus-10 with him on the court, minus-17 with him off the court.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's standout performance in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: That guy Stephon Castle is the best player in this game.
quotes.quote: If you were just parachuted in from another planet and not known anything about who any of the people were, you would have said, 'That guy Stephon Castle is the best player in this game.' And I thought he was the reason, as great as Wembanyama was, I would have said, 'That guy Stephon Castle is the reason San Antonio won.'

quotes.speaker: Monica McNutt
quotes.summary_phrase: Supporting cast contributions to Wembanyama's success
quotes.excerpt: Supporting cast showing up to make life easier for Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: It's talked about in terms of the supporting cast showing up to make life easier for Wembanyama, right? Like Castle had 18 in the first half, he had five big points in the fourth quarter. But you also look at Harper who was getting to the rim and getting downhill. Fox obviously had the big basket late. I think to me though, there's so much that you can pick from in this game. And perhaps you credit the Spurs' defense because they do come up with 21 points off of Knicks turnovers.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' poor ball security and early game struggles
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks opened ice cold. They threw the ball away.
quotes.quote: The Knicks opened ice cold. They threw the ball away. You can't even, almost can't, not to take any credit away from anything, but there were some possessions early for those of you who may not have seen the beginning of the game, the Knicks just threw the ball away regardless of the defense.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Spears
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of a packed crowd on player routine and focus
quotes.excerpt: When a crowd is packed way before, it's just natural. You start engaging with people.
quotes.quote: I will say like, going to a lot of NBA games and playing in games, when the crowd starts to come in, you're usually at a point where you're getting a real good lather, you're getting ready to, and then you go back in a huddle in the locker room and you come out and you're ready to warm up and play the game. When a crowd is packed way before, it's just natural. You start engaging with people. People start saying what's up. It's way more distracting. The routine is way different for the players.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Greenberg's observation of Stephon Castle's wardrobe changes
quotes.excerpt: When did he change? And why?
quotes.quote: The one big question I have for Stephon Castle is that when he came in an interview who were watching yesterday morning, when he came in and jumped in on our show as he sometimes does, which we love, and then did first take, he was wearing a very noticeable pink suit. Then at the game last night, he was wearing a blue suit. And so my question is, when did he change? And why? I'm still reeling from Stephon Castle's warm-up suit. I respect the kid, I have no idea. That was a look, right? And he walked in, you can't help but notice it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst explains the wardrobe changes of players
quotes.excerpt: It's the garden, baby. You gotta make it a moment.
quotes.quote: Jeremy Lynn, who is my new colleague here at ESPN who I love working with, he wore one thing to NBA today, he put on Knicks gear for when he was on celebrity row, and then after the game when he was back to doing television with Scott Van Pelt, was back in the suit. Iman Shumpert, I walked into the building yesterday, he was searched by secret service wearing a green and black very beautiful ensemble. When the game started, he was wearing a head-to-toe bright orange suit. It looked like Walt Frazier and Spike Lee came together to collab on what he was wearing. Where did these outfit changes come from? I have no idea. It's the garden, baby. You gotta make it a moment. Come on, everybody's watching.
